import.title: Import
import.description: Interactions and the predefined L1/L2 taxonomy for the current project. Once both are imported, the dialog closes. Data stays on this computer.
import.drop: Drop files here or click to browse
import.formatIntro: One interaction is one conversation between a customer and an agent. Only the conversation text is required; everything else is optional.
import.formatCsv: either one row per conversation with a transcript column (lines like “Customer: …” / “Agent: …”), or one row per message with conversation ID, speaker and text. Columns are detected automatically and can be mapped after upload.
import.formatTxt: one file per conversation with “Customer:” / “Agent:” lines, or several conversations in one file split by a separator line (e.g. ---).
import.formatSpeakers: Speaker names such as customer, client, caller, Kunde or agent, advisor, Mitarbeiter are recognised. Lines without a speaker count as customer text.
import.formatOptional: Optional metadata: conversation ID, channel (voice, chat, email, …), segment, language, timestamp, queue. Without an ID, one is generated.
import.formatDuplicates: Conversation IDs that already exist in the project are skipped, so you can import additional files later.

fieldHints.transcript: Whole conversation in one cell (Customer: … / Agent: …)
fieldHints.speaker: Turn-level files: one row per message

taxImport.intro: The L1/L2 taxonomy is the fixed frame of the analysis: every intent is first assigned to an L2 category, and the AI then builds L3/L4 categories below it. Its language becomes the analysis language.
taxImport.ruleLevels: Only levels 1 and 2. L1 categories have parent_id null; every L2 needs the id of an existing L1 as parent_id.
taxImport.ruleIds: id, label and level are required. IDs must be unique and stay stable; they appear in exports.
taxImport.ruleDescriptions: Write one clear sentence per description: the local LLM uses label and description to decide which L2 an intent belongs to.
taxImport.ruleL3L4: L3 and L4 are never imported; they are discovered from the data.
taxImport.ruleWhen: Import before the first analysis. Once interactions are assigned, reset the analysis first (Settings → Reset analysis). The import replaces the current L1/L2 structure.
taxImport.current: Current structure: {l1} L1 / {l2} L2 categories · analysis language: {lang}
taxImport.none: This project has no L1/L2 taxonomy yet.
taxImport.promptTitle: No structure at hand? Create one with a prompt
taxImport.promptStep1: Copy the prompt and fill in the parts in square brackets (industry, channels, topics).
taxImport.promptStep2: Run it in an AI tool approved in your organisation, or locally with Ollama (e.g. ollama run qwen3:8b).
taxImport.promptStep3: Save the answer as a .json file, check the categories and descriptions, and upload it here.
taxImport.promptPrivacy: The prompt only needs a description of the business. Do not paste customer data or transcripts into external AI tools.
taxImport.prompt:
You are an expert in contact center customer service taxonomies.
Create a two-level base taxonomy (L1/L2) for the following customer service:

Company / industry: [e.g. health insurance]
Contact channels: [e.g. phone, chat, email]
Key products and topics: [e.g. membership, contributions, benefits, online services]

Rules:
- 4 to 8 L1 categories (domains), each with 2 to 6 L2 categories (topics).
- L2 categories do not overlap and together cover all typical customer requests.
- No specific individual requests: the finer levels L3/L4 are discovered later from the conversations.
- Every category gets a one-sentence description: which customer requests belong in it?
- Labels and descriptions in English.
- IDs: L1 as "L1-XXX", L2 as "L2-XXX-YYY" (upper case, unique).

Answer only with valid JSON in exactly this format:
{"name": "...", "categories": [
  {"id": "L1-XXX", "level": 1, "parent_id": null, "label": "...", "description": "..."},
  {"id": "L2-XXX-YYY", "level": 2, "parent_id": "L1-XXX", "label": "...", "description": "..."}
]}

export.title: Export results
export.description: Exports reflect the current saved taxonomy and assignments, including manual corrections.
export.excelText: Four sheets: Taxonomy, Interaction Assignments (one row per intent), Review Queue, Taxonomy Changes.
export.csvText: A single sheet, or all sheets as a ZIP archive.
export.jsonText: Complete export including all taxonomy nodes (with retired/merged), assignments and history.
export.languageNote: Headers, sheet names and status values follow the interface language. Category names and AI texts are in the analysis language ({lang}). The JSON export stays machine-readable in English.
export.reportText: Insights with KPIs, top intents including notes, charts, overlap check and the complete taxonomy overview, branded with your logo.
export.reportBusy: Creating report… notes may first be written by the local LLM.
export.reportError: The report could not be created: {error}

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Model server, analysis parameters and maintenance for the current project.
settings.testHint: Runs a real inference and embedding request.
settings.thresholds: Match existing category ≥ {match} · cluster cohesion ≥ {cluster} · overlap flagged ≥ {merge} (cosine similarity)
settings.autoAcceptHint: Only clearly non-conflicting new L3/L4 nodes. Merges and splits always require review.
settings.privacy: Transcript text is sent to the Ollama server for inference. If it runs on another machine, use only synthetic data or an approved, secured network connection for real customer data. No other external service receives data.
settings.confirmResetAnalysis: Remove all analysis results of this project (intents, L3/L4 categories, proposals, reviews)? Imported interactions are kept.
settings.confirmClear: Delete all imported interactions and analysis results of this project?
settings.languageHint: Detected automatically from the imported L1/L2 taxonomy. Intents, new L3/L4 categories and descriptions are generated in this language.
settings.brandingHint: PNG, JPG or WebP. Shown in the app header and in the PDF report header.

gt.title: Quality check against the sample's known answers
gt.text: The synthetic sample dataset ships with the true intent of every conversation. The AI never sees these labels; they are only used here to show how well the discovered taxonomy matches them. Not shown for your own data.
gt.l2RecallHint: Share of true intents whose expected L2 was assigned in the conversation
gt.l4PurityHint: Share of conversations in each L4 that share its dominant true intent
gt.note: This check only works for the synthetic sample. It measures how well the AI recovers known intents; it does not prove that a taxonomy is complete, and 100 conversations are too few for that anyway.
